entities.name: Roughskin dogfish
entities.fact: The roughskin dogfish is a small shark of the continental slopes that lives at depths of many hundreds of metres.

entities.name: Longnose velvet dogfish
entities.fact: The longnose velvet dogfish lives on the continental slopes of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans, hundreds of metres below the surface.

entities.name: Great lanternshark
entities.fact: The great lanternshark is a deep North Atlantic shark with light-producing organs on its underside, found thousands of metres down.

entities.name: Blackbelly lanternshark
entities.fact: The blackbelly lanternshark is a small deep-water shark that glows faintly from light-producing organs on its dark belly.

entities.name: Southern lanternshark
entities.fact: The southern lanternshark lives on the deep continental slopes of the Southern Hemisphere and carries light-producing organs on its belly.

entities.name: Smalleye pygmy shark
entities.fact: The smalleye pygmy shark is one of the smallest sharks alive, a deep-water species of the Indo-Pacific that stays under 25 centimetres long.

entities.name: Bigeye sixgill shark
entities.fact: The bigeye sixgill shark has six gill slits on each side and lives on slopes and seamounts at depths of hundreds of metres.

entities.name: Ghost catshark
entities.fact: Ghost catsharks, the genus Apristurus, are slim, dark sharks with dozens of species that live on the deep sea floor.

entities.name: Iceland catshark
entities.fact: The Iceland catshark is a pale, slender shark of the North Atlantic that lives on deep slopes far below the reach of sunlight.

entities.name: Lollipop catshark
entities.fact: The lollipop catshark of the eastern Pacific has a broad rounded head and a thin tapering body and lives on the deep sea floor.

entities.name: Blackmouth catshark
entities.fact: The blackmouth catshark has a dark lining to its mouth and lives on the deep sea floor of the north-east Atlantic and Mediterranean.

entities.name: Shortspine spurdog
entities.fact: The shortspine spurdog is a small dogfish with a spine in front of each dorsal fin, living on deep slopes and seamounts in many seas.

entities.name: Knifetooth dogfish
entities.fact: The knifetooth dogfish has blade-like lower teeth for cutting chunks from its prey and lives on deep slopes of the eastern Atlantic.

entities.name: Draughtsboard shark
entities.fact: The draughtsboard shark of New Zealand is named for the chequered pattern of bands and blotches on its back.

entities.name: Varied catshark
entities.fact: The varied catshark hides among rocks and reefs off southern Australia and is patterned with dark spots and bands.

entities.name: Grey bamboo shark
entities.fact: The grey bamboo shark is a slim, nocturnal shark that rests on shallow Indo-Pacific reefs and sandy seabeds by day.

entities.name: Banded wobbegong
entities.fact: The banded wobbegong is a flattened ambush shark of Australian reefs, camouflaged by bold bands and fringes of skin around its mouth.

entities.name: Blonde ray
entities.fact: The blonde ray is a large skate of the north-east Atlantic with pale, sandy colouring and a pattern of small dark spots.

entities.name: Spotted ray
entities.fact: The spotted ray lives on sandy seabeds of the north-east Atlantic and is covered in small dark spots.

entities.name: Undulate ray
entities.fact: The undulate ray is named for the wavy dark lines that run across the pale upper side of its body.

entities.name: Starry ray
entities.fact: The starry ray, also called the thorny skate, is covered in sharp, star-shaped thorns on its back and tail.

entities.name: Big skate
entities.fact: The big skate of the north-east Pacific carries a pair of large eye-like spots on its wings and can grow over two metres long.

entities.name: Winter skate
entities.fact: The winter skate of the north-west Atlantic has an eye-like spot on each wing and lives on sandy and gravelly seabeds.

entities.name: Chupare stingray
entities.fact: The chupare stingray lives in the shallow waters of the Caribbean and nearby western Atlantic.

entities.name: Longnose stingray
entities.fact: The longnose stingray has a long pointed snout and lives in coastal waters of the western Atlantic from the Gulf of Mexico to Brazil.

entities.name: Estuary stingray
entities.fact: The estuary stingray lives in estuaries, bays and tidal rivers along the east coast of Australia.

entities.name: White-blotched river stingray
entities.fact: The white-blotched river stingray lives only in Brazil's Xingu River and has a dark disc covered in pale blotches.

entities.name: Bigtooth river stingray
entities.fact: The bigtooth river stingray is a freshwater ray found in the Tocantins-Araguaia river basin of Brazil.

entities.name: Cortez round stingray
entities.fact: The Cortez round stingray is a small, round-bodied ray found only in the Gulf of California.

entities.name: Mekong freshwater stingray
entities.fact: The Mekong freshwater stingray lives in the Mekong river system of south-east Asia.

entities.name: Sparsely-spotted stingaree
entities.fact: The sparsely-spotted stingaree is a small round-bodied ray of southern Australian waters that lives on sandy seabeds.

entities.name: Yellowback stingaree
entities.fact: The yellowback stingaree is a small stingray of the eastern Australian coast with a yellowish back.

entities.name: Smalleye stingray
entities.fact: The smalleye stingray is a large Indo-West Pacific ray with tiny eyes that lives on soft seabeds.

entities.name: Banded stingaree
entities.fact: The banded stingaree is a small, round-bodied ray of southern Australia with a pattern of dark bands across its back.

entities.name: Rosette river stingray
entities.fact: The rosette river stingray is a freshwater ray of the Amazon basin marked with a pattern of dark-edged rosettes.

entities.name: Smoothback river stingray
entities.fact: The smoothback river stingray is a freshwater ray found in rivers of the Amazon and Orinoco basins.

entities.name: Ross Sea killer whale
entities.fact: The Ross Sea killer whale, or Type C, is a small Antarctic form of killer whale that hunts Antarctic toothfish around the sea ice.

entities.name: Pack ice killer whale
entities.fact: The pack ice killer whale, or Type B, hunts seals around Antarctic ice floes and often looks yellowish from a film of diatoms on its skin.

entities.name: Subantarctic killer whale
entities.fact: The subantarctic killer whale, or Type D, has a tiny eye patch and a rounded head and was first recognised from a mass stranding in New Zealand in 1955.

entities.name: Lahille's dolphin
entities.fact: Lahille's dolphin is a large bottlenose dolphin of estuaries and coasts in southern Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina.

entities.name: Burrunan dolphin
entities.fact: The Burrunan dolphin lives in sheltered bays and lakes of southern Australia, such as Port Phillip Bay and the Gippsland Lakes.

entities.name: Orinoco river dolphin
entities.fact: The Orinoco river dolphin is the pink river dolphin of the Orinoco basin in Venezuela and Colombia.

entities.name: Mahakam river dolphin
entities.fact: The Mahakam river dolphin is a tiny, critically endangered freshwater population of Irrawaddy dolphins in the Mahakam River of Borneo.

entities.name: Mekong dolphin
entities.fact: The Mekong dolphin is a critically endangered freshwater population of Irrawaddy dolphins that lives in a stretch of the Mekong between Cambodia and Laos.

entities.name: Eastern spinner dolphin
entities.fact: The eastern spinner dolphin of the eastern tropical Pacific often swims above schools of yellowfin tuna.

entities.name: Dwarf spinner dolphin
entities.fact: The dwarf spinner dolphin is a small form of spinner dolphin that lives in the shallow seas of south-east Asia and northern Australia.

entities.name: Central American spinner dolphin
entities.fact: The Central American spinner dolphin is a coastal form of spinner dolphin found off the Pacific shores of Central America.

entities.name: Coastal spotted dolphin
entities.fact: The coastal spotted dolphin is a nearshore form of the pantropical spotted dolphin found along the Pacific coast of the Americas.

entities.name: Guadalupe fur seal
entities.fact: The Guadalupe fur seal was thought to be extinct until a small colony was rediscovered at Guadalupe Island, Mexico, in the 1950s.

entities.name: Juan Fernandez fur seal
entities.fact: The Juan Fernandez fur seal was believed extinct after heavy hunting until it was found again in the 1960s on Chile's Juan Fernandez Islands.

entities.name: Subantarctic fur seal
entities.fact: The subantarctic fur seal breeds on remote islands of the southern Indian and Atlantic oceans, such as Amsterdam Island and Gough Island.

entities.name: South American fur seal
entities.fact: The South American fur seal breeds along the coasts of Peru, Chile, Argentina and Uruguay and the Falkland Islands.

entities.name: New Zealand fur seal
entities.fact: The New Zealand fur seal, known to Maori as the kekeno, breeds around New Zealand and the coasts of southern Australia.

entities.name: Saimaa ringed seal
entities.fact: The Saimaa ringed seal lives only in Finland's freshwater Lake Saimaa and numbers just a few hundred animals.

entities.name: Black guillemot
entities.fact: The black guillemot is a black seabird with white wing patches and bright red feet that nests along rocky Arctic and subarctic coasts.

entities.name: Ross's gull
entities.fact: Ross's gull is a small, pink-tinged Arctic gull that breeds in Siberia and spends the winter near the edge of Arctic pack ice.

entities.name: Common eider
entities.fact: The common eider is a sea duck of Arctic and northern coasts whose soft down has long been used to fill quilts.

entities.name: Marbled sea snake
entities.fact: The marbled sea snake feeds almost entirely on fish eggs and has tiny fangs compared with most other sea snakes.

entities.name: Yellow sea snake
entities.fact: The yellow sea snake is a large, yellow-and-black banded sea snake of the Indian Ocean and western Pacific that gives birth to live young at sea.

entities.name: Arabian Gulf sea snake
entities.fact: The Arabian Gulf sea snake lives in the shallow waters of the Persian Gulf and nearby seas and bears live young in the water.

entities.name: Dwarf sea snake
entities.fact: The dwarf sea snake is a small, true sea snake of Indo-Pacific coastal waters that spends its whole life in the sea.

entities.name: Viperine sea snake
entities.fact: The viperine sea snake is a true sea snake of Asian coastal waters with a flattened, paddle-like tail for swimming.

entities.name: Jerdon's sea snake
entities.fact: Jerdon's sea snake is a true sea snake of Indo-Pacific coastal waters that spends its whole life in the sea.

entities.name: New Caledonian sea krait
entities.fact: The New Caledonian sea krait hunts eels on coral reefs but returns to land to rest, digest and lay its eggs.

entities.name: Olive-headed sea snake
entities.fact: The olive-headed sea snake is a true sea snake of the coral reefs and seagrass beds of northern Australia and New Guinea.

entities.name: Black-headed sea snake
entities.fact: The black-headed sea snake is a slender true sea snake of south-east Asian coastal waters.

entities.name: Spectacled sea snake
entities.fact: The spectacled sea snake is a true sea snake that lives in the shallow waters off northern Australia.

entities.name: Small-headed sea snake
entities.fact: The small-headed sea snake has a tiny head on a slim neck and lives in the shallow waters off northern Australia.

entities.name: Ijima's sea snake
entities.fact: Ijima's turtle-headed sea snake feeds on fish eggs and lives around reefs of the Ryukyu Islands and Taiwan.

entities.name: Maori octopus
entities.fact: The Maori octopus is a large octopus of New Zealand and southern Australian waters.

entities.name: Blue-lined octopus
entities.fact: The blue-lined octopus is a small, highly venomous octopus of Australian waters whose bright blue lines flash when it is threatened.

entities.name: Mototi octopus
entities.fact: The mototi octopus is a small Indo-Pacific octopus that lives on shallow, silty seabeds.

entities.name: Atlantic longarm octopus
entities.fact: The Atlantic longarm octopus can mimic a swimming flatfish as it glides over sandy seabeds.

entities.name: Webfoot octopus
entities.fact: The webfoot octopus is a small octopus of East Asian waters that is caught and eaten in Japan, Korea and China.

entities.name: Fourhorn octopus
entities.fact: The fourhorn octopus lives on muddy seabeds of the eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

entities.name: Pale octopus
entities.fact: The pale octopus is a small octopus of the south-eastern Australian coast that lives on sandy and muddy seabeds.

entities.name: Southern sand octopus
entities.fact: The southern sand octopus lives on sandy seabeds of southern Australia.

entities.name: Ornate octopus
entities.fact: The ornate octopus is a night-active Indo-Pacific octopus marked with pale stripes.

entities.name: Sevenstar flying squid
entities.fact: The sevenstar flying squid is a Southern Ocean squid that is an important food for albatrosses and seals.

entities.name: Boreal clubhook squid
entities.fact: The boreal clubhook squid is a common squid of Arctic and subarctic waters that is eaten by whales and seals.

entities.name: Magister armhook squid
entities.fact: The magister armhook squid is an abundant squid of the North Pacific, eaten by seals, seabirds and fish.

entities.name: Purpleback flying squid
entities.fact: The purpleback flying squid has a glowing patch on its back and can glide above the surface of tropical seas.

entities.name: Northern shortfin squid
entities.fact: The northern shortfin squid of the north-west Atlantic lives only about a year and is fished in large numbers.

entities.name: Lesser flying squid
entities.fact: The lesser flying squid lives in the north-east Atlantic and the Mediterranean, mostly close to the seabed.

entities.name: Southern calamari
entities.fact: The southern calamari is a large, fast-growing squid of southern Australian and New Zealand waters that is caught for food.

entities.name: Common clubhook squid
entities.fact: The common clubhook squid has sharp hooks on its tentacle clubs and lives in warm and temperate oceans worldwide.

entities.name: New Zealand arrow squid
entities.fact: The New Zealand arrow squid is the target of one of the country's biggest squid fisheries.

entities.name: Swordtip squid
entities.fact: The swordtip squid is a Pacific squid caught for food in Japan and elsewhere in East Asia.

entities.name: Atlantic brief squid
entities.fact: The Atlantic brief squid is a small squid of the western Atlantic that can tolerate the low salt levels of estuaries.

entities.name: Gould's squid
entities.fact: Gould's squid is an arrow squid of southern Australian waters that is fished commercially.

entities.name: Golden king crab
entities.fact: The golden king crab lives on cold, deep seabeds of the North Pacific and is fished for its sweet meat.

entities.name: Blue swimmer crab
entities.fact: The blue swimmer crab has paddle-shaped back legs for swimming and is caught for food around Australia and the Indo-Pacific.

entities.name: Halloween crab
entities.fact: The Halloween crab is a black-and-orange land crab of Pacific Central America that returns to the sea to release its eggs.

entities.name: Western rock lobster
entities.fact: The western rock lobster is a spiny lobster of Western Australia that supports one of the country's most valuable fisheries.

entities.name: Southern rock lobster
entities.fact: The southern rock lobster is a spiny lobster of southern Australia and New Zealand that shelters in rocky reefs.

entities.name: Banana prawn
entities.fact: The banana prawn is a pale, curved prawn of the Indo-West Pacific that is caught in huge numbers in northern Australia.

entities.name: Brine shrimp
entities.fact: Brine shrimp are tiny crustaceans that thrive in extremely salty lakes and lagoons where fish cannot survive.

entities.name: Amano shrimp
entities.fact: The Amano shrimp is a small freshwater shrimp of Japan that is kept in aquariums for eating algae.

entities.name: White-spotted jellyfish
entities.fact: The white-spotted jellyfish is a bell-shaped jelly speckled with white spots that has spread far beyond its Pacific home.

entities.name: Purple-striped jelly
entities.fact: The purple-striped jelly of the Californian coast has long frilly arms and often lives alongside the jellies it feeds on.

entities.name: Textile cone
entities.fact: The textile cone is a cone snail patterned like woven cloth that harpoons its prey with venom and can be dangerous to people.

entities.name: Bluefire jellyfish
entities.fact: The bluefire jellyfish is a small, bluish relative of the lion's mane that is common around the coasts of north-west Europe.

entities.name: Giant phantom jelly
entities.fact: The giant phantom jelly is a rarely seen deep-sea jelly with four enormous ribbon-like arms that trail for several metres.

entities.name: Caribbean box jelly
entities.fact: The Caribbean box jelly lives among mangrove roots and has 24 eyes, some of which can form images.

entities.name: Beroe comb jelly
entities.fact: Beroe is a sack-shaped comb jelly with no tentacles that swallows other comb jellies whole.

entities.name: English sole
entities.fact: Despite its name, the English sole is a flatfish of the north-east Pacific, caught from Alaska to California.

entities.name: Rock sole
entities.fact: The rock sole is a Pacific flatfish that lives on gravelly and rocky seabeds from California to the Bering Sea.

entities.name: Flathead sole
entities.fact: The flathead sole is a large-mouthed flatfish of the North Pacific, found from California to the Bering Sea.

entities.name: Butter sole
entities.fact: The butter sole is a flatfish of the north-east Pacific that lives on sandy and muddy seabeds.

entities.name: Yellowtail flounder
entities.fact: The yellowtail flounder is a flatfish of the north-west Atlantic with rusty-red spots and a yellow edge to its tail.

entities.name: Kamchatka flounder
entities.fact: The Kamchatka flounder is a large flatfish of the deep North Pacific and Bering Sea.

entities.name: Senegalese sole
entities.fact: The Senegalese sole lives in the eastern Atlantic from the Bay of Biscay to West Africa and is farmed in southern Europe.

entities.name: Greenback flounder
entities.fact: The greenback flounder is a flatfish of southern Australia and New Zealand that lives in estuaries and shallow bays.

entities.name: Gulf flounder
entities.fact: The gulf flounder lives on sandy and muddy seabeds from the Carolinas to the Gulf of Mexico.

entities.name: Japan Trench snailfish
entities.fact: The Japan Trench snailfish is a soft-bodied fish that lives in the Japan Trench at depths of more than 6,000 metres.

entities.name: Atacama snailfish
entities.fact: The Atacama snailfish lives in the Atacama Trench off Peru and Chile, thousands of metres deeper than most fish can survive.

entities.name: Belyaev's snailfish
entities.fact: Belyaev's snailfish is a hadal snailfish of the trenches of the north-west Pacific.

entities.name: Bathycallisoma
entities.fact: Bathycallisoma schellenbergi is a large scavenging amphipod of the deepest Pacific trenches.

entities.name: Bathykermadeca hadalis
entities.fact: Bathykermadeca hadalis is an isopod first found in the Kermadec Trench, living deeper than 6,000 metres.

entities.name: Valettietta gracilis
entities.fact: Valettietta gracilis is a slender amphipod that lives in trenches of the Pacific, far below the reach of sunlight.

entities.name: Galatheanthemum hadale
entities.fact: Galatheanthemum hadale is a sea anemone recorded from the deep trenches of the Pacific, below 6,000 metres.

entities.name: RMS Empress of Ireland
entities.fact: The ocean liner Empress of Ireland sank in the St Lawrence River in 1914 after a collision in fog, with the loss of more than 1,000 lives.

entities.name: HMS Royal Oak
entities.fact: The battleship HMS Royal Oak was torpedoed by a U-boat at Scapa Flow in 1939, and her wreck is now a protected war grave.

entities.name: SS President Coolidge
entities.fact: The former luxury liner SS President Coolidge sank off Vanuatu in 1942 after striking friendly mines and is now a famous dive site.

entities.name: USS Saratoga
entities.fact: The aircraft carrier USS Saratoga was sunk in the 1946 atomic bomb tests at Bikini Atoll and now lies upright in the lagoon as a dive site.

entities.name: HMS Repulse
entities.fact: The battlecruiser HMS Repulse was sunk by Japanese aircraft off Malaya in December 1941, along with HMS Prince of Wales.

entities.name: RMS Rhone
entities.fact: The steamer RMS Rhone sank in a hurricane off Salt Island in the British Virgin Islands in 1867 and is now a popular dive site.

entities.name: Alvinella caudata
entities.fact: Alvinella caudata is a close relative of the Pompeii worm that lives on the chimney walls of East Pacific Rise vents.

entities.name: Neomphalus
entities.fact: Neomphalus fretterae is a limpet-like snail that grazes on bacteria around vents of the Galapagos Rift and East Pacific Rise.

entities.name: Shinkaia crosnieri
entities.fact: Shinkaia crosnieri is a squat lobster of Okinawa Trough vents that carries chemosynthetic bacteria on its bristles.

entities.name: Mirocaris fortunata
entities.fact: Mirocaris fortunata is a small shrimp that swarms around hydrothermal vents on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

entities.name: Ophioctenella acies
entities.fact: Ophioctenella acies is a brittle star that gathers in dense swarms around hydrothermal vents of the Mid-Cayman Rise in the Caribbean.

entities.name: Pachycara thermophilum
entities.fact: Pachycara thermophilum is an eelpout that lives around hot vents on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

entities.name: Gigantopelta chessoia
entities.fact: Gigantopelta chessoia is a large vent snail found at hydrothermal vents on the East Scotia Ridge in the Southern Ocean.

entities.name: Segonzacia mesatlantica
entities.fact: Segonzacia mesatlantica is a crab that lives around hot vents on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

entities.name: Nautilocaris saintlaurentae
entities.fact: Nautilocaris saintlaurentae is a shrimp that lives around hydrothermal vents in the Lau Basin of the south-west Pacific.

entities.name: Austinograea williamsi
entities.fact: Austinograea williamsi is a crab of hydrothermal vents in the western Pacific.

entities.name: Cyanagraea praedator
entities.fact: Cyanagraea praedator is a crab found around hot vents of the East Pacific Rise.
